contentIssue.badRowAnyColumn: This row was skipped because one of its columns holds something a “{type}” row can’t use. Correct the cell and save the file — the rest of the file loaded normally.
contentIssue.badRowColumn: This row was skipped because the column {columns} holds something a “{type}” row can’t use. Correct the cell and save the file — the rest of the file loaded normally.
contentIssue.badRowColumns: This row was skipped because the columns {columns} hold something a “{type}” row can’t use. Correct the cells and save the file — the rest of the file loaded normally.
contentIssue.badTagValue: The tag “{name}” has to be a whole number, and this row gives it something else — so it is ignored, and the item behaves as if the tag weren’t there at all. Write it as {name}:12, or remove it.
contentIssue.duplicateId: Two entries share the id “{id}” under the same source, so only the first one is used and this one is ignored everywhere in the app. Give one of them a different id, or delete the copy.
contentIssue.malformedLocaleColumn: This column looks like a translation, but Charnik can’t read a language code out of it, so the column is ignored. Translation columns are written name_<code> or text_<code> — name_uk, text_de.
contentIssue.noSubclassRows: This class hands out a subclass at level {level}, but no subclass in this edition names it — so a character reaching that level is asked for a choice with nothing in it. Add the subclass rows, or clear “subclass_level”.
contentIssue.oversizedFile: This file is bigger than the {cap} MB Charnik reads for one content file, so it was skipped. A content CSV is normally far smaller than that — check it isn’t a backup, an export, or a damaged file. If it really is content, split it into several files; every file in the folder is loaded.
contentIssue.partialTranslation: Half-translated into {language} — the parts that are missing show in English until you fill them in (Compendium ▸ Edit compendium ▸ Translate).
contentIssue.resourceOptionUngranted: This option spends a resource nothing gives the character, so it never appears. Check the id against the feature that grants the pool.
contentIssue.resourceOptionUngrantedSuggested: This option spends a resource nothing gives the character, so it never appears. Did you mean {options}?
contentIssue.resourceUngranted: This names a resource nothing gives the character, so the name is never used. Check the id against the feature that grants the pool.
contentIssue.resourceUngrantedSuggested: This names a resource nothing gives the character, so the name is never used. Did you mean {options}?
contentIssue.schemaNewer: This file was written by a newer version of Charnik than the one you are running. Its rows were loaded as they are, so anything the newer version added is ignored — update Charnik to read the file fully.
contentIssue.schemaOlder: This file uses an older layout that Charnik has no way to bring forward, so its rows were loaded exactly as written. If entries from it look wrong, open one in the app and save it again.
contentIssue.unknownDeclaredType: This file says it holds a kind of content this version of Charnik doesn’t know, so none of its rows were loaded. Either the type is misspelled, or the file arrived with content newer than the app — updating Charnik would then read it.
contentIssue.unknownDeclaredTypeSuggested: This file says it holds a kind of content this version of Charnik doesn’t know, so none of its rows were loaded. Either the type is misspelled (did you mean {options}?), or the file arrived with content newer than the app — updating Charnik would then read it.
contentIssue.unknownFileType: This version of Charnik can’t tell what this file holds, so it was skipped — nothing else in the folder is affected. If you wrote it, name it after the kind of content it has (spells_mine.csv, feats_mine.csv) or add a first line saying so: #content-type: spell. If it arrived with a content pack, it is probably a kind of content a newer Charnik adds; updating the app will read it.
contentIssue.unresolvedBaseItem: This item says it is built from another item that doesn’t exist under the same source, so it inherits nothing — no damage, no properties, no weapon category. Check the id for a typo, or add the base item to a CSV in the same pack.
contentIssue.unresolvedBaseItemSuggested: This item says it is built from another item that doesn’t exist under the same source, so it inherits nothing — no damage, no properties, no weapon category. Did you mean {options}?
contentIssue.unresolvedJoin: This row puts a spell on a class’s list, but no “{kind}” in this edition has that id — so the row does nothing. Check the id for a typo, or whether the row’s “systems” column names the edition that “{kind}” is in.
contentIssue.unresolvedJoinSuggested: This row puts a spell on a class’s list, but no “{kind}” in this edition has that id — so the row does nothing. Did you mean {options}?

demo.title: Heads up — this demo only ships the free SRD content
demo.body: Charnik is in active development. We can only include the SRD — the part Wizards of the Coast released for free (CC-BY). The rest of D&D belongs to them, not us, so a lot of it legally can't be here out of the box: Artificer, Aasimar, the Beholder, most subclasses, and loads of spells & monsters. But nothing holds you back — make your own homebrew and, with the flexible CSV system, add whatever you want: from species and classes to spells. You can also download the full desktop app for your computer — it keeps all your data local and needs no internet connection.

effectIssue.armorBlocksCasting: Not proficient with {category} armour — spellcasting blocked.
effectIssue.dependencyCycle: This effect needs its own result before it can work out its own result, so Charnik cannot apply it — it is left out of the sheet. Rewrite it so it depends on something else.
effectIssue.duplicateClassFeature: Two content packs both provide this class feature. Charnik applied it once, not twice — pick which copy you want in Settings ▸ Content to make the choice explicit.
effectIssue.noPreparedCount: Charnik doesn’t know how many spells {class} prepares at level {level} in {system}, so it shows none — this edition gives no formula to work it out from. Add the count for that level to the class’s casting table in your content.
effectIssue.pluginFailed: This part of the sheet is worked out by a plugin, and the plugin did not return a usable answer — so it contributes nothing. Nothing else on the sheet is affected. Fix the plugin, then press “Retry plugins”.
effectIssue.rolledAbilityScore: An ability score changes by a fixed amount, never by a roll, so this effect was left out.
effectIssue.unknownCondition: Something tried to apply a condition called “{id}”, but this edition has no such condition — so nothing was applied. Add it to a conditions CSV, or correct the name.
effectIssue.unknownConditionSuggested: Something tried to apply a condition called “{id}”, but this edition has no such condition — so nothing was applied. Did you mean {options}?
effectIssue.unknownTarget: Nothing on the sheet is called “{target}”, so this effect changes nothing. Check the spelling in the row’s effects column.
effectIssue.unknownTargetSuggested: Nothing on the sheet is called “{target}”, so this effect changes nothing. Did you mean {options}?
effectIssue.unreadableAbilityChange: Charnik could not work out how much this changes the ability score by, so it was left out.
effectIssue.unreadableGuard: Charnik cannot tell whether the condition in front of this effect is met, so the effect is not applied.
effectIssue.unreadableOptionCondition: Charnik cannot tell when this option is meant to be available, so it is always offered. Check the condition on the row.
effectIssue.unreadableOptionCost: This option does not say how much it costs in a way Charnik understands, so it is not offered. The cost has to be a whole number, or “x” for “you choose how many”.
effectIssue.unreadableOptionEffect: Charnik could not work out what this option heals or rolls, so it is offered with the formula exactly as written.
effectIssue.unreadableResourceMax: Charnik could not work out how many uses this gives, so it is not shown in the resource tracker. Correct the count in the row and it will appear.
effectIssue.unrollableValue: This should offer something to roll, but its formula does not work out to dice or a number — so no roll is offered.

info.base_item_id: The id of the ordinary item this one is built from, e.g. “longsword” for a +1 Longsword. Everything left blank here is taken from it.
info.material: Material component text, e.g. “a pinch of sulfur and bat guano”.
info.higher_level: What changes when cast with a higher-level slot.
info.effects: Auto-calc effects, “;”-separated. Format kind:target±amount. e.g. flat_bonus:ac+1; damage_sensitivity:resist:fire; grant_proficiency:skill.stealth. Leave blank if none.

general.critNote: Either way the flat modifier is never doubled. A single roll can be switched to the other method in the roller, where a table usually rules on it.

health.allClear: All loaded content is healthy — no problems found.
health.blurb: What Charnik noticed while reading your content files. The app keeps working either way — but anything listed here is missing from the app, or isn’t doing what its file says it should. Each entry names the file to open and what to change in it.
health.editingModeBlurb: While this is on, a CSV you edit on disk has its hash re-stamped automatically and neither startup prompt appears. Turn it off and Charnik asks before touching a file again.
health.groupDerive: Things that didn’t work out on “{name}” (this sheet only)
health.groupDriftBlurb: Their contents no longer match the fingerprint recorded inside them. Nothing is broken and your edits are being used — but until the fingerprint is re-stamped, Charnik leaves these files alone rather than replacing them when their content pack updates.
health.groupErrors: Did not load — this content is missing from the app
health.groupJoins: Points at a resource that doesn’t exist
health.groupLints: Effects that look like a slip of the pen
health.groupLintsBlurb: These work — Charnik is only pointing out things that are usually a typo, like a d7 or two branches of one formula that return different kinds of value. Written for whoever authored the row.
health.groupMeta: Files that don’t say where they came from
health.groupMetaBlurb: These files load and work normally — but without a source and a licence, Charnik can’t credit their author or tell you what you may share. It offers to fill this in when it starts, or you can add the two lines yourself at the top of the file.
health.groupWarnings: Loaded, but something in it is off
health.title: Content health

packs.title: Content updates
packs.desc: Content packs are folders of CSVs — the shipped SRD is simply the one Charnik bundles. Charnik can check whether a pack’s repository has newer rules data, so a correction reaches you without a new app version. Only GitHub repository links work for now. Checking is one request per repository per day at most; APPLYING an update is always your click.
packs.desktopOnly: Content updates are a desktop feature — the web demo always serves the content of its own deploy.
packs.chipTitle: {count, plural, one {# content pack has} other {# content packs have}} newer rules data. Open Settings to see what would change.
packs.none: No content packs are registered yet.
packs.filesPreserved: {count} file(s) you edited will be kept as they are
packs.rowsRemoved: {count} entries would DISAPPEAR from your content
packs.draftsAffected: Unfinished edits that would be left with nothing to edit: {who}
packs.packTooLarge: “{pack}” is too big to download: {files} files, {mb} MB (limit {maxFiles} files, {maxMb} MB).
packs.carriesPlugins: This pack also contains plugins: {list}. They arrive switched off and need your review.
packs.changesPlugins: This update rewrites plugin code: {list}. Applying it stops those plugins until you approve the new code, and any stats they calculate will change.
packs.installGone: “{pack}” is no longer among the packs Charnik found in that repository — the listing it was offered from has moved on. Check for updates again, then install it from the fresh list. Nothing was changed.
packs.applyGone: There is no longer an update waiting for “{pack}” — it was already applied, or a newer check found it had been withdrawn. Nothing was changed.
packs.applyBadRepo: Charnik can no longer tell where “{pack}” comes from, so it has nothing to download from. Its recorded link is {repo}. Remove the pack’s repository and add it again. Nothing was changed.
packs.hostUnsupported: Charnik can’t check {repo} — update checks currently work with GitHub repository links only.
packs.tooManyPacks: {repo} offers {packs} content packs — more than Charnik will list at once (limit {max}). Nothing was changed; a repository this large is more likely a mistake in the link than a collection you meant to browse.
packs.repoTooBig: {repo} holds too many files for GitHub to list in one go, so Charnik only ever sees part of it — and acting on half a list could delete content that is still there. Nothing was changed.
packs.sourceChanged: “{pack}” now claims to be a different source (“{from}” → “{to}”). That makes it a NEW pack, not an update: every entry would be renamed and any character using them would lose the link. Nothing was changed — install it as a separate pack instead.
packs.sourceClaimed: “{pack}” publishes its entries as “{source}” — the same name “{owner}” already uses here. That name is what the app shows as an entry’s origin, so this pack’s entries would look like they came from “{owner}”, and the two would share one on/off switch. That’s normal for a fork of the same content, and a red flag for anything else. Nothing was installed.
packs.saveFailed: Charnik couldn’t save your content-pack settings. Pins, repository links and the update mode are still in force for now, but they will be gone when you close the app — and a pinned pack could then be updated. This is almost always the data folder being full, read-only, or on a drive that has gone away: check it, then flip any pack setting to try saving again. ({message})
packs.noPacksFound: No content packs found in {repo} — a pack is a top-level folder holding CSV files.
packs.nameTaken: The folder “{name}” already belongs to another pack, so this one goes in a folder of its own. Change the name if you like.
packs.folderTaken: The folder “{name}” is already in use — pick another name.
packs.badFolderName: “{name}” can’t be used as a folder name.
packs.renameBundled: “{name}” is one of the packs the app ships, so it keeps its folder — that is how the app knows to keep it up to date and to offer it back if you delete it.
packs.readyOffline: Downloaded and ready — applying it works offline
packs.ownRepoHint: Charnik’s own packs — the SRD ones it ships with — live at
packs.missingLabel: Deleted, but still in the app
packs.missingNote: Not on your disk. The copy inside the app can go back any time — no internet needed.
packs.contentMoved: “{path}” changed on the server while it was being downloaded. Nothing was written; check again in a moment.
packs.localChanged: These files changed on your disk after this update was prepared: {files}. Nothing was written, because the summary you approved no longer describes them. Check for updates again to see the current picture.
packs.rowsWouldVanish: This update deletes {count, plural, one {# entry} other {# entries}} from inside the files it rewrites. Nothing was written yet — check the list below, then apply again to accept it.
packs.undoDone: “{pack}” is back to the version it had before the last update.
packs.uninstallWarn: Deletes its files from your disk, and the {count} entries it gives you with them. Characters using any of those go blank there. You can get it back any time from {repo}.
packs.uninstallWarnEmpty: Deletes its files from your disk. Characters using anything from it go blank there. You can get it back any time from {repo}.

plugins.title: Plugins
plugins.desc: Community plugins extend effects with sandboxed code — from the plugins/ folder in your data folder, or shipped inside a content pack. Every plugin is off until you review and enable it, wherever it came from.
plugins.webOnly: Plugins run in the desktop app only.
plugins.none: No plugins found. Put a plugin folder under plugins/ in your data folder and refresh.
plugins.forgetTitle: Forget this plugin — enabling it again asks for your review

consent.title: Enable this plugin?
consent.sandbox: Runs sandboxed: no files, no network, no app access. It can only compute numbers for your sheet.
consent.name: Name
consent.author: Author
consent.warning: Only enable plugins from authors you trust.

sources.blurb: Turn whole sources or individual files on and off. A row shows only when both its source and its file are enabled. This just hides them from browsing and creation — nothing is deleted, and flipping a switch back brings everything straight back.
sources.title: Content sources

storage.blurb: Where Charnik keeps your characters and content on this device. Moving copies everything to the new folder, checks every file arrived, and only then removes the old one.
storage.title: Data location
storage.webNote: On the web version your data lives in this browser’s storage — there’s no folder to move. Use Export to take a copy with you.

themes.blurb: Build your own colour theme by overriding the design tokens. Clone Dark or Light, tweak the swatches, and it applies live. Each theme is a JSON file (in your data folder) you can share or hand-edit.
themes.title: Themes

snapshots.title: Snapshots
snapshots.blurb: Charnik keeps a few automatic copies of every character — two checkpoints while you play and one per launch. Put one back if a sheet is lost or wrong.
snapshots.none: No snapshots yet. The first is taken the next time this character is saved.
snapshots.confirmBody: The sheet as it is now is replaced by the snapshot from {when}. The other snapshots are kept, so this is not the only way back.
snapshots.failed: That snapshot could not be restored —
